2.text: with the Reindeer people, the rule of distribution is somewhat more complicated.

3.text: When thong-seals are abundant, each man takes a hide, beginning with the

4.text: master. When they are scarce, the middle part of each hide is cut up and

5.text: wound into two rolls of thong of medium thickness. The rest of the hide is

6.text: cut into eight parts and distributed among the crew as material for boot-soles.

7.text: The thongs are given to the men one after another, beginning with the master,

8.text: as described. In modern times, instead of this rule of distribution, the hides

9.text: of thong-seals are often taken by those hunters who have killed the respective

10.text: animals, which are thus excluded from the common stock. This new way is

11.text: not approved by public opinion; still it is more and more frequently adopted.

12.text: With the whale, the meat, as has been mentioned, belongs to the whole

13.text: village, generally to whoever wants to take part in the carving. The bones

14.text: of the jaw are taken by the one who first noticed the whale. The whalebone

15.text: is divided equally among all the participants of the hunt, and is distributed

16.text: by the master, who reserves the best and longest slabs for himself. The

17.text: man who dealt the mortal blow, usually the one who sits at the prow, has

18.text: the right to choose his portion next after the master. When the boat comes

19.text: ashore, the master will take some of the smaller slabs, which are not used in

20.text: trade, and distribute them among the onlookers.

21.text: I was told that in former times, as many as fifty years ago, after each

22.text: successful catch, a large part of the best whalebone was distributed among

23.text: all the inhabitants of the village. The price of the whalebone was lower, and

24.text: whales more abundant. The rich people had also an old supply not yet sold

25.text: to the Americans. At present good whalebone is too valuable and rare to

26.text: be thus distributed. This last information was given me by a native, for my

27.text: guidance. In most cases, however, the whale is killed, not by a single boat,

28.text: but by two, three, or several boats. One of the boats, that has acted fore-

29.text: most, is considered as the “principal boat,” the others are only “assistant boats.”

30.text: Then the whalebone is divided along the middle line into two equal parts,

31.text: which are called “whalebone-sides” (tiˊnqäl). The principal boat takes one half.

32.text: The other half is divided among the assistant boats; and each boat distributes

33.text: its portion among its crew. When a whale has drifted ashore, the meat and

34.text: blubber are carved and taken by all present; but the whalebone belongs, as a

35.text: rule, to the one who first noticed the whale. “Be it a small girl five years

36.text: old, she must take all the whalebone,” thus say the Chukchee. “To act
